subtype: Approach: telling a parent even when unsure [Revision]
passage: On the road home from the well, a stranger on a motorbike had asked Aditi to come along with him to see something. Her legs had locked, and she said nothing until he rode off. All evening at the village house she stirred the dal and kept quiet, ashamed that she had frozen. Then she went to Amma Sangeeta, who was folding clothes. "Something happened." Sangeeta set the clothes down and listened to all of it. "You did nothing wrong, Aditi. Thank you for telling me." They told her father that night, and her teacher the next morning. Now Aditi walks with a neighbour girl, and the family made a plan she could say by heart.

qa.q: Who did Aditi tell about what happened?
Why did Aditi keep quiet at first, and how did she feel?
qa.a: She felt ashamed that she had frozen, which is why she stirred the dal and said nothing all evening.

qa.q: What could Aditi do if a stranger asks her to come along again, and why?
qa.a: She could say no loudly, move toward people and tell an adult, as the family plan says, because telling early keeps more people watching out for her. 🤍

qa.q: How does Sangeeta respond to Aditi?
qa.a: Sangeeta puts down the clothes, listens to all of it, and tells Aditi she did nothing wrong, so Aditi feels heard rather than blamed.

grounding: A girl who froze in front of a stranger feels ashamed, then tells her mother, and the family adds a plan.

subtype: Approach: telling a parent even when unsure [Revision]
passage: On the way back from the park in Madrid, a woman Rosa didn't know had asked her to come and look at some kittens in her car. Rosa hadn't moved. She hadn't said anything either. She had just stood there, frozen, until a dog barked and the woman walked off. At home Rosa said nothing. She felt ashamed of freezing and afraid she'd be in trouble. But at dinner she couldn't eat. Finally she said, "Mamá, something happened." Her mother, Lucia, put down her fork and listened without interrupting. "You're not in trouble. Freezing is normal. Thank you for telling me." That night Lucia called the police, and they made a family plan: shout no, run to a shop, and always tell.

qa.q: What did the woman ask Rosa to come and look at?
Why did Rosa say nothing at first when she got home?
qa.a: She felt ashamed of freezing and afraid she would be in trouble.

qa.q: What does the family plan add, and what else could help?
qa.a: It gives Rosa clear steps: shout no, run to a shop and tell; practising it aloud could make it easier to do if she freezes again.

qa.q: How does Rosa's news look to Lucia?
qa.a: Lucia listens calmly and is careful to reassure Rosa, while taking it seriously by calling the police that night.

grounding: It shows a girl who froze when a stranger asked her to come along, hiding it at first out of shame, then telling her mother and the family making a plan.

subtype: Approach: telling a parent even when unsure [Revision]
passage: At the badminton academy, Alka was quiet all through practice. In the changing room her friend Ishita asked what was wrong. Alka hesitated. "A man outside the gate asked me to come with him to his car. I just froze. I didn't say anything. He left when the coach came out." "Did you tell anyone?" "No. I feel stupid." "You're not stupid. You have to tell your mum." When her mother arrived at reception, Alka told her, voice shaking. Her mother knelt down. "You're safe. It's not your fault. Freezing happens." She went straight to the academy manager, who checked the gate camera and called the police. That night the family agreed on a code word.

qa.a: He left when the coach came out.

qa.q: How did Alka feel about freezing?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and stupid, which is why she didn't want to tell anyone at first.

qa.q: What did Ishita do well, and what else could have helped?
qa.a: Ishita listened and pushed Alka to tell a trusted adult; she could also have gone with Alka to tell the coach right away.

qa.q: How does the news look to Alka's mother?
qa.a: Her mother is calm and reassuring, telling Alka it isn't her fault, and acts at once by going to the academy manager.

grounding: It shows a girl who froze when a stranger asked her to come, hiding it at first and then deciding to tell her mother, after which the family makes a plan.
